annotations.text:
ROUND 2 — WITH LIGHT IN IT

Round 1 was sterile because I designed from the constraints doc, and its own words — restraint, quiet competence, no gradients, light ledger — walked straight back into the G3 trap.

What every reference you sent actually shares: a DARK ground and ONE object lit from within. Your own G1 had it too — the luminous navy hero. I stripped out the only thing that made any of them feel alive.

STOKE is fire. The app should feel lit, not audited.

Corrected rule: cheap flat gradient pills are slop. Atmospheric radial light that builds depth is craft.

A · HEARTH — warm room, one ember

Cream ground, but the money card is a dark ember lit from inside — orange bloom top-left, live flame glyph, glowing figure. The white card below catches warm light off it.

ARGUES: the app is a warm place; money is the fire in the middle of it.

CLOSEST to your G1 instinct, executed with real depth instead of a flat navy slab. Safest of the four and still has a pulse.

B · OBSIDIAN — the whole app is the studio

Full dark. 82px money glowing. An 84px breathing record trigger on the home screen. This is your session-paused reference applied to the entire product.

ARGUES: recording is not a mode you enter, it is what this app IS.

COSTS: the two-surface doctrine dies — dark stops meaning recording. Worth it? Genuinely open. It is the most striking of the four.

C · PRESS — editorial, printed, warm

104px money. Real paper grain. Devanagari at 30px as a pull-quote. Hairline rules instead of cards. One glowing record button as the single hot spot.

ARGUES: the script is the product, so typography carries the whole thing.

COSTS: least information per screen, and the type does not scale down gracefully to 320px. Most distinctive on a portfolio shot.

D · CONSTELLATION — coverage as lights coming on

The district grid from round 1, but as embers on a dark map. Lit districts glow amber. Yours pulses. CTA reads 'Light up a district.'

ARGUES: you are not grinding tasks, you are lighting up a country. This is the coverage reframe made emotional instead of a spreadsheet.

COSTS: money is demoted to a header pill. The biggest product bet — and the screenshot nobody else has.

STILL MIXABLE

D's constellation could be the hero inside A's warm room. C's 104px money could sit on B's dark ground.

The live question is no longer palette — it is HOW MUCH DARK.

A = a lit object in a warm room
B = dark everywhere
C = light, one hot spot
D = dark, many small lights

Tell me which one has a pulse and I will push that one further.
